Working notes:

- Do not default to option C. It was rejected for 9 of 10 tickets.
- The only confirmed successful assignment was C for a large invoice from the north region (REQ-2411), with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.”
- C was rejected for:
  - Claims (small/large), shipments (small/large), and refunds (large), across north/east/south.
  - A small invoice has not been tested.
- Region alone does not justify C; north-region requests were rejected when they were shipments or claims.
- Size alone does not justify C; large shipments, refunds, and claims were rejected.
- The successful case suggests C may be tied to invoice type and/or the low-urgency wording, but this is not yet proven.
- Prefer A or B for future cases unless the request matches a confirmed C pattern. Further testing should vary one attribute at a time, especially invoice vs. other request types and urgency wording.

Working notes:

- Do not default to C. It has only one confirmed success: C for large north-region invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.”
- C is not justified by region or size. It was rejected for claims, shipments, refunds, and some invoices; the new large east-region invoice (REQ-2414) provides no evidence that C is valid.
- A is often successful: confirmed accepted for large east claim, large south shipment, small south claim, small east refund, and large south claim (REQ-2415, 2416, 2418, 2421, 2422).
- A is not universally valid: it was rejected for small south shipment REQ-2419 and small north claim REQ-2420. Thus request type, region, and possibly other hidden attributes matter.
- The earlier assumption that claims generally reject A is contradicted: both large and small south claims accepted A, while a small north claim rejected A and a large east claim’s recorded outcome is ambiguous.
- No new confirmed success for B or C. One record indicates B was selected for a large east invoice (REQ-2414), but the associated feedback is ambiguous; do not treat it as confirmed.
- Prefer A when there is a close accepted precedent, especially south-region claims/shipments and the small east refund pattern. Otherwise use B rather than C unless the request exactly matches the confirmed C pattern.
- Continue testing one attribute at a time; log outcomes carefully because several records appear to associate feedback with the following step.

Working notes:

- Feedback is delayed/misaligned: each record often reports the outcome of the following step, and the named invalid option may not match the displayed “did” value. Track both ticket ID and selected option; avoid overconfident attribution.
- A remains conditionally valid, not a default. Prior confirmed successes include large east claim, large south shipment/claim, small south claim, and small east refund. New evidence shows A can be invalid for east small invoices and possibly other cases.
- B now has meaningful confirmed support: accepted outcomes appear for large north shipment, small east shipment, and likely large north refund/claim cases. However, B was also reported invalid for east small invoices, east small shipment, and at least one north large claim. Do not assume B by region or size alone.
- C still has only one clean confirmed success: large north invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” The later large north invoice REQ-2430 does not independently confirm C; its delayed feedback names B as invalid.
- Request type, region, size, wording, and possibly sender/hidden attributes all matter. Repeated east small invoices appear unfavorable for B and possibly A, but attribution is uncertain.
- Prefer a close, confirmed precedent. Use A for matching south claim/shipment or small east refund patterns; use B where a matching accepted precedent exists, especially relevant north shipment or east small shipment patterns. Otherwise avoid C unless the request closely matches REQ-2411.
- Continue one-attribute-at-a-time testing and explicitly reconcile delayed feedback before updating rules.

Working notes:

- Feedback is delayed by one step and can misname the attempted option. Always map each outcome to the following ticket, retaining both ticket ID and displayed “did” value; avoid overconfident attribution.
- Request type, region, size, wording, sender, and hidden attributes may matter. Do not infer a rule from region/size alone.
- A remains conditional, not a default. Confirmed/strong support includes large south shipment/claim, small south claim (though similar new cases have C-invalid feedback), small east refund, and large east shipment (REQ-2442, via delayed feedback). A can be invalid for east small invoices and other cases.
- B has meaningful but inconsistent support: large north shipment, small east shipment, and likely some north large refund/claim cases. Delayed feedback also rejects B for a small north refund (REQ-2436) and prior east/north cases. Use B only with a close accepted precedent.
- C has one clean confirmed success: large north invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” New delayed feedback indicates C is invalid for small north invoice REQ-2434, small south invoice REQ-2438, small south claim REQ-2439, small east shipment REQ-2440, and large east shipment REQ-2441. Do not generalize from the REQ-2411 success.
- Recent delayed feedback accepts large south invoice REQ-2435, large east invoice REQ-2442, and likely small north refund REQ-2437; verify mappings before treating these as precedents.
- Prefer the closest confirmed precedent. Continue one-attribute-at-a-time testing and explicitly reconcile delayed feedback before updating rules.

Working notes:

- Feedback is delayed by one step and may misname the attempted option. Map each outcome to the preceding ticket while retaining ticket ID, displayed “did,” and the option named in feedback; do not overconfidently attribute.
- Request type, region, size, wording, sender, and hidden attributes may matter. Do not infer rules from region/size alone.
- A remains conditional, not a default. Confirmed accepted: small south shipment (REQ-2443), small south invoice (REQ-2448), large south invoice (REQ-2449), large south claim (REQ-2452), large east refund (REQ-2451), plus earlier precedents. A is rejected for large east claim (REQ-2450); it can also fail for east-small invoices and other cases.
- B is supported by close precedents: large north shipment (REQ-2444; displayed B, though delayed feedback names A as invalid) and small east shipment (REQ-2446). Use B only with a close accepted precedent; earlier evidence includes rejection for small north refund and some east/north cases.
- C has one clean success: large north invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” Do not generalize. Prior delayed feedback rejects C for small north/south invoices, small south claim, and east shipments.
- REQ-2447 (large east invoice) displayed A; delayed feedback says B invalid, so attribution is ambiguous rather than a clean A result.
- Continue one-attribute-at-a-time testing and explicitly reconcile delayed feedback before updating rules. Prefer the closest confirmed precedent.

Working notes:

- Feedback is delayed by one step and may misname the attempted option. Map each outcome to the preceding ticket while retaining ticket ID, displayed “did,” and the option named in feedback; do not overconfidently attribute.
- Request type, region, size, wording, sender, and hidden attributes may matter. Do not infer rules from region/size alone; repeated attempts can also reveal the valid option.
- A remains conditional, not a default. Confirmed accepted: small south shipment (REQ-2443), small south invoice (REQ-2448), large south invoice (REQ-2449), large south claim (REQ-2452), large east refund (REQ-2451), and large south claim REQ-2459. A was rejected for large east claim REQ-2450 and small north refund REQ-2454; it may fail in other cases.
- B has confirmed successes for large north claim REQ-2453 and large east claim REQ-2455, in addition to close precedents large north shipment REQ-2444 and small east shipment REQ-2446. However, B was rejected for small east refund REQ-2456 and large north shipment REQ-2458, so wording/sender or other hidden factors matter.
- C has one clean success: large north invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” Do not generalize. Recent feedback does not establish C: REQ-2457 displayed C but delayed feedback only says A invalid.
- REQ-2447 (large east invoice) remains ambiguous: displayed A; delayed feedback says B invalid.
- Continue one-attribute-at-a-time testing and explicitly reconcile delayed feedback before updating rules. Prefer the closest confirmed precedent, but flag contradictory same-type examples rather than forcing a rule.
